data.reasoning: The package is a standard AUR binary package (-bin) that downloads pre-built executables from the project's official GitHub releases page (github.com/someoneonsmile/clip). data.disagreement_analysis: The disagreement was caused by a tool error, not a substantive security concern. Report 1 (qwen/qwen3-235b-a22b-2507) ended inconclusive due to an HTTP 400 API error when auditing .SRCINFO, while Report 2 (deepseek/deepseek-v4-flash) successfully completed and found both files safe. Report 3 (openrouter/free) is marked advisory:true and does not count as a vote. The two models that successfully completed their analysis agreed the package is safe.
coverage_issues: Report 1 (qwen) failed to audit .SRCINFO due to API error (HTTP 400 BadRequestError), resulting in inconclusive verdict
learnings: Tool errors (API failures) should not cause entire audits to be marked inconclusive when critical files have been successfully assessed - implement graceful degradation

Models correctly identify that SKIP checksums for binary packages are standard practice and not inherently malicious - this pattern should be documented as a known-safe pattern to reduce false positive risk
For -bin packages, models should focus on verifying that source URLs point to the declared upstream repository and that no executable code runs during sourcing - both models did this correctly
